newsitem.title: UK: Dlr/yen regains ground after tankan sparks stumble.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/yen regains ground after tankan sparks stumble.

text.p: The dollar recovered some ground above 113 yen in early Europe after stumbling more than one yen overnight as the Bank of Japan's quarterly tankan survey showed big manufacturers growing surprisingly optimistic in June.
But analysts said while the tankan's key diffusion index was strong, the yen's assault on the dollar could be stalled by less optimistic sentiment for non-manufacturers and smaller firms.
"The headline number may say one thing but the underlying numbers point to the fact that the domestic economy remains depressed," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank.

At 0745 GMT dollar/yen was trading at 113.67, above overnight lows of 113.30 yen, but still down against late Europe levels of 114.78/83 yen. Dollar/mark, slapped lower by dollar/yen, stood at 1.7191/96 against 1.7256/63.

The BoJ's diffusion index for big manufacturers, a key gauge of business confidence, rose to plus seven in June from plus two in March, when the previous survey was conducted. Consensus forecasts had been were for fall of 0.5.
The diffusion index for non-major manufacturers, however, slipped to minus seven in June from minus six in March and the index for small manufacturers improved only slightly.

"The only sector that saw a big pick-up was major manufacturers. They are the exporters, so the tankan highlights that Japan is still relying on increasing exports and its domestic economy is going nowhere at the moment," said Commerzbank's Ferridge.

A senior BoJ official on Wednesday echoed these remarks, saying the Japanese economic recovery has not strengthened as much as the improvement in business sentiment among major manufacturers, and that it was difficult to say that the economic recovery had become stronger just by the improvement in the diffusion index (DI) for major manufacturers alone.
"I don't think we can say that the economic recovery has become as strong as the improvement in the major manufacturers' DI," the official told Reuters.
Japanese financial markets, however, were shaken on the heels of the tankan survey with bond and euroyen futures tumbling and Tokyo stocks rising.
Dlr/yen was also tripped-up in Asian dealings.

Some analysts said while mixed, the tankan's strong headline diffusion index seems also to have increased market expectations of a rate rise later this year, even though the recovery was due to exports.

"We have been bullish on the Japanese economy for some months now, we expect the GDP growth of 2.9 percent in calendar 1997. And our view on interest rates is that we expect the BoJ to hike the official discount rate in the fourth-quarter of this year," said Klaus Kusber, currency analyst at Kleinwort Benson.
But, Kusber said rather than change the bank's view on rates, the tankan had confirmed them.
Dollar/mark was softer in Europe, dampened by cable's rally and dollar/yen's slide, said traders.
The market is now focusing on U.S. durable goods orders for May due at 1230 GMT, with orders forecast to show a rise of 0.6 percent against a rise of 1.3 percent in April.
